text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but this modest gain masks a brutal week—the stock has fallen 5.5% over two weeks and dropped sharply yesterday. The decline accelerated on November 4th as oil prices weakened (US crude at $99.64 today, down from recent highs), and that weakness continued today despite the company releasing quarterly earnings and a financial report. When oil prices fall, it directly cuts into the cash flow and profits of producers like ConocoPhillips, even if the company's underlying operations remain solid.

The political backdrop is also weighing on the sector. News of incoming Democratic scrutiny of energy deals—including questions about U.S. involvement in Venezuela and mineral concessions—has created uncertainty for oil majors, particularly those with international exposure. This regulatory headwind, combined with softer oil markets, has kept investor sentiment cautious even as the company reported results.
